customer-john: Hi team — our nightly CI deploys started failing last night around 02:15 UTC. Jobs that call the Redwood API suddenly get 403 / 401 errors halfway through long-running steps. This only started after we rolled the vault auto-rotate policy last week. Can you help?

support-bot: Thanks for reporting, @customer-john. I've created a ticket (SUP-202603-1123) and notified on-call. Can you paste the failing logs and the timestamp of the failing run? :eyes:

customer-john: Logs pasted below (sanitized). Run ID 2026-03-11T02:14:55Z. Error shows both 401 and 403 depending on step: 

```
[2026-03-11T02:14:56Z] step: model-embedding -> POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings
[2026-03-11T02:14:56Z] headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
[2026-03-11T02:14:56Z] response: 401 Unauthorized {"error":"token_expired","message":"token expired at 2026-03-11T00:15:00Z"}
[2026-03-11T02:18:03Z] step: long-batch-infer -> POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
[2026-03-11T02:18:03Z] response: 403 Forbidden {"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"missing: inference.invoke"}
```

The job runs a 45m batch; looks like tokens are valid at start and then expire mid-run. The 403 shows missing permission for a later sub-step that uses a different endpoint.

maria-support: Thanks @customer-john — useful snippets. Two potential issues: (1) token TTL / rotation (looks like expiry mid-run), (2) scope/role differences between endpoints. Are you using a single service account token for all CI steps or per-step tokens?

customer-john: Single token issued to our CI service account (ci-build-bot). We recently changed vault auto-rotate from 24h -> 2h for all service tokens (policy change). We thought CI would refresh, but our runner doesn't request a new token mid-job.

alex-platform: @maria-support and @customer-john — I reproduced quickly using their setup. Using a long job with the vault-rotated token shows expiry halfway through. Repro steps: 

1) create token with 2h TTL via vault rotate policy (simulated)
2) start a job that does a few short requests, then sleeps 30m, then runs a long generate call
3) observe 401 at the long generate call timestamp.

curl repro (sanitized):
```
TOKEN=eyJ...REDACTED
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-medium","input":"hello"}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate | jq .
```

Response when token expired: 
```
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{"error":"token_expired","message":"token expired at 2026-03-11T00:15:00Z"}
```

alex-platform: Also saw a different behavior when we used a token created with reduced scopes: earlier steps (embeddings) were allowed because they use scope `embeddings:create`, but the later generate call requires `inference:invoke` and that permission was not attached to the CI token. That explains the 403. So this is a combined TTL + least-privilege mismatch problem.

anna-sre: Important: our vault rotation policy change was rolled on 2026-03-04 and affected any token without the "no-rotate" tag. The CI team didn’t tag ci-build-bot. @maria-support can confirm. The quick remediation path is either: 
- make CI runner refresh tokens mid-job (preferred long-term), or
- issue a longer-TTL token for the CI service account or a dedicated deploy token that is exempted from auto-rotate, or
- move CI to OIDC short-lived tokens with on-demand refresh (recommended by security).

maria-support: Customer asked for the minimum viable fix to get nightly deploys back on. They want to avoid big infra changes right now. What’s a low-risk workaround we can apply quickly?

tony-sec: Low-risk path we can approve immediately: create a new dedicated service account `ci-deploy-bot` with minimal roles, issue a token with a TTL of 8h (28800s) and mark it as "rotation-exempt" for the next 2 weeks while CI is updated. Security caveats: we must log creation and rotate the token manually after the window, and create an auditable ticket. Long-term we move to OIDC.

maria-support: @tony-sec ack. Customer is ok with an 8h token temporarily. @customer-john can you confirm you only use that token from your CI runners and it will be stored in your vault path that we can exempt?

customer-john: Yes. We can drop the new token into vault at `secret/ci/ci-deploy-bot` and give the runner read-only access. We'll update the runner to refresh at the start of each job. Mid-job refresh not possible in the short term.

alex-platform: Actionable steps I will run now (will paste commands): 

1) create dedicated service account + role binding
```
# create service account
redwoodctl iam service-accounts create ci-deploy-bot --display-name "CI Deploy Bot"
# bind minimal role
redwoodctl iam roles bind --service-account ci-deploy-bot --role inference.invoker --resource project:acme-prod
```
2) issue token with 8h TTL and tag exempt
```
redwoodctl tokens create --service-account ci-deploy-bot --ttl 28800 --scopes inference:invoke,embeddings:create --meta rotation=exempt | jq .token
```
3) drop into vault path and allow read to CI role
```
vault kv put secret/ci/ci-deploy-bot token=$(cat token.txt)
vault policy write ci-read - <<EOF
path "secret/data/ci/*" { capabilities = ["read"] }
EOF
vault write auth/approle/role/ci-runner policies=ci-read
```

alex-platform: I'll also add a short-term instrumentation check in our platform to emit a warning whenever a token TTL < job duration is used (log + slack alert).

maria-support: Great. For the 403 insufficient_scope: note we added `embeddings:create` and `inference:invoke` to the token scopes above so both endpoints will work. Please confirm your job doesn't require admin-level scopes.

customer-john: Confirmed — those two scopes are sufficient. We do not need management scopes.

anna-sre: Post-mortem notes for infra: we should update the rotation rollout checklist to include CI service account tagging, and add a guardrail that refuses to flip global rotation policy without a sweep through known CI roles. Filing infra-ops issue INFRA-2026-42.

tony-sec: Security follow-up: we require OIDC migration plan in 30 days. I'll own the migration RFC and include the required audience claim and token exchange flow. For now the 8h exempt token is approved under SUP-202603-1123.

maria-support: Work items (summary):
• alex-platform: create ci-deploy-bot, bind roles, generate 8h token, drop to vault (in progress)
• customer-john: update CI runner secret path and restart nightly job (pending)
• anna-sre: add rotation-tagging sweep + INFRA-2026-42 (todo)
• tony-sec: OIDC migration RFC (30d)

maria-support: I'll keep this thread open until we verify a successful nightly run tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

support-bot: SUP-202603-1123 updated: status=investigating, priority=high, assignees=[alex-platform, maria-support]
